text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London maintained slight losses by the close, ignoring a new rally in New York. Traders said London's failure to make any breakthrough on the upside reflected the persistent lack of buying power. The benchmark May position traded from $1,540 and $1,564 a tonne to end the day $5 down at $1,559 a tonne. July finished down $7 at $1,565 a tonne. It was the most active contract as some players rolled out of the May positions ahead of the first delivery day on May 1.

The May/May arbitrage against New York still stood at a wide 122 cents and July/July at 103 cents. Robustas are still well supplied and the market is now bracing for what some traders said was an earlier-than-usual Indonesian main harvest. Arabica futures in New York ended sharply higher, led by steep gains in the spot contract, as near term supply worries were reignited by news Colombia had closed coffee registrations for May and June shipments, dealers said.

Spot May delivery ended up 6.90 cents/lb at 196.00 cents/lb after trading from 197 to 186.20. Second month July settled 4.80 cents/lb higher at 177.00 cents/lb, while the back months closed up 0.95 to 4.00 cents/lb.

The May/July switch, a barometer of nearby availability rose to a hefty 19.00 cents, up from 16.90 cents at the close on Friday. Meanwhile, traders await the Green Coffee Association of New York's monthly stock data due after the close of business on April 15 to better gauge the US supply situation. Traders expect an increase of 250,000 to 300,000 bags from February's 1.54 million bags. But despite the expected rise in GCA coffee stocks there are still concerns that many Latin American countries, who shipped heavily in the last two months to take advantage of the higher futures prices, may have little coffee left to sell.
After Monday's close CSCE reported certified coffee stocks were off 250 60-kg bags to 80,828 bags as of April 11. There were no bags pending grading, the exchange added.

COLOMBIA - The National Coffee Growers' Federation told private exporters on April 14 that it was closing registrations for May/June coffee shipments with immediate effect, industry sources said. Federation officials could not be reached for comment. But several exporters told Reuters that they had been formally notified of the move in a statement from the federation. Registrations for shipments by private exporters in April, May and June were opened by the federation on March 7.

COLOMBIA - The chief of Colombia's National Coffee Growers' Federation, Jorge Cardenas, said the country produced just 10 million 60-kg bags of coffee in April 1996 through March 1997, down from about 14 million in the same period in 1995/96. He declined to speculate on the impact of the drop on total production in the 1996/97 coffee year, but he said output between April and September was seen totalling not more than about 4.5 million 60-kg bags.

Cardenas added, the 4.5 million figure included expected production of 3 million bags during the so-called 'mitaca' harvest beginning in April and ending in June. Cardenas gave no reason for the sharp decline in production between April 1996 and last month, but heavy rains at the start of the year were widely seen as a factor that would cut into overall production figures. Cardenas also said the federation had drawn since last October on about 1.5 million bags of coffee in its inventories, leaving it with a current total of 5 million bags.

BRAZIL - Workers at the key port of Santos will go on strike at 0700 local/1000 GMT on April 15 for an indefinite period, the president of the Santos Stevedores Union said. The strike will include all categories of workers at the port and has been called in protest against the lack of progress in negotiations with steel firm Companhia Siderurgica Paulista (Cosipa) over a labor dispute. Representatives of the National Stevedores Union will meet on April 15 and the strike could spread to national level by the next day, said the union's president Abelardo Fernandes.

SWEDEN - Coffee imports in October 1996 amounted to 202,667 60-kg bags, up from 140,563 bags imported in October 1995. This brought cumulative imports in the first ten months of 1996 (January/October) up to 1.770 million bags, more than 25 per cent up on the tonnage imported in the like period the previous year. Total imports in calendar year 1995 reached 1.648 million bags against 1.893 million bags in 1994. Major suppliers of green coffee in January/October 1996 were Brazil (374,800 vs 386,900 bags), Colombia (371,800 vs 315,900 bags) and Germany (292,000 vs 170,200 bags).

Coffee exports in January/October 1996 reached 184,486 bags, a rise of 10 percent on the volume exported in the corresponding year-ago period. Total exports in 1995 amounted to 204,682 bags against 223,947 bags in 1994. Sweden exports most of its coffee in the form of roast and ground with the USA (106,000 vs 98,200 bags) and Finland (36,500 vs 27,200 bags) being the main markets.
